speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment as we move towards further easing measures in the community, how will the social distancing ambassadors be aided to enforce rules on the ground as there will be more grey areas on when and how to mask on.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These measures are critical to safeguarding public health and protect ourselves and each other, even as we gradually open up our economy and social settings.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Even though caseloads are currently low, we must not let our guard down.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will need to stay nimble and calibrate our measures appropriately.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are briefed by their team leaders and supervisors on adjustments to the measures and provided reference material through their mobile devices.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are also deployed in teams of at least two, where a more experienced officer will be partnered with a newer one to provide support and guidance.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mask wearing will remain an important measure for public health to protect ourselves and those we come into contact with.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: You should also keep your mask on when seated before you start consuming your food or drink or before you begin your workout.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have been able to contain the COVID-19 situation with the co-operation of the community and business operators.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I urge everyone to continue to play your part in adhering to these safe distancing measures and to co-operate with the Safe Distancing Ambassadors and Enforcement Officers, so that we continue to keep community transmission of COVID-19 under control.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I think we are not disputing the need to put on masks and also to have safe distancing.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: But I suppose the hardest part is the duty of the safe Distancing Ambassadors because everybody has to play their part.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: But I have already received quite some feedback from residents, for example, at a very popular hawker centre in the market.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The point is, the Safe Distancing Ambassadors use judgement to give advsiories, for example, when exactly must they put on the mask.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Some people say immediately; once they put down their chopsticks and utensils, they need to immediately put on the mask; and there were Safe Distancing Ambassadors who told them as such.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: There are others who used their discretion and felt that some people can some conversation before they put on the mask.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: As a result of these varying differences, I think it makes it very challenging on the ground, especially as we move towards Phase 3 – I am not sure when that is – and you increase the number of people who can come out to dine.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I think this is the biggest challenge that people would face on the ground, including those in exercise corners as well.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I just wanted to ask the Minister what other measures can be done to aid the Safe Distancing Ambassadors and also for the public not to make things difficult for the Safe Distancing Ambassadors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I agree that sometimes, it is difficult for the work of the Safe Distancing Ambassadors to enforce all the rules.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But of course, the Safe Distancing Ambassadors are not everywhere at all times to ensure that.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, a lot depends on all of us, as customers, as patrons at hawker centres to do our part.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ultimately, the rules are really to support our own health, to support our neighbours' health, our family's health.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, my point is, the Safe Distancing Ambassadors are there to remind people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Very often, we would like to see that with some advice and with some reminders, patrons will put back their masks and the majority of them do.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I just want to reiterate that the rules are quite clear.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As informed by science, the more we are able to protect ourselves through masks, the safer we are.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is advised that everybody put on your mask as much as you can, as soon as you can.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Even as we relax and as more activities are being allowed, I think the wearing of masks is still important for us to observe.
